answer.rationale: memory_73 (targeted promotional pricing) is least supported for long-term qualified revenue because discounting SMB segments may optimize short-term acquisition but systematically damages unit economics and creates price-floor expectations that harm sustainability. The memory reports acquisition and revenue lift but omits critical data: cohort retention curves, CAC payback periods, and whether acquired customers stayed as full-price, qualified revenue. Price-sensitive segments acquired through promotions typically show lower LTV and higher churn post-discount, making them poor candidates for sustainable revenue. memory_44 (sales-assisted enterprise flows) rates highest because enterprise sales-assisted motion directly correlates with larger contract values, longer retention, and qualified revenue fundamentals. memory_31 and memory_57 rate 4 because signup simplification and referral incentives both strengthen the funnel from known causes (reduced friction, word-of-mouth quality signals), though they lack explicit retention/LTV measurement. memory_86 and memory_91 (onboarding and activation messaging) rate 3 because faster time-to-value improves early metrics but the memory does not measure whether these improvements persisted in cohort retention or expanded TAM among quality segments; activation lift without qualified segment focus risks optimizing volume over value.
